Hochschule für Gestaltung building, Ulm

Max Bill’s building for the Ulm School of Design (1953–1955): low volumes of bare concrete on a hillside, with ribbon windows in wooden frames.

Source
Wikipedia: Ulm School of Design
Creator
Max Bill
Made
1953–1955 (inaugurated 2 October 1955)
Style
Ulm School (partial fit; agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Austere, rational, calm
Evidence
Inspected two Wikimedia Commons photographs as 1280 px thumbnails: HfGUlmbuilding 5.jpg by Trop86 (30 May 2021, CC BY-SA 4.0) and HfG Ulm Main Entrance by Christian Gänshirt (July 2014, CC BY-SA 4.0). These are recent views, so later repairs may differ from the 1955 state. No image is stored.
Reviewed
2 October 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Wikipedia: “In 1953 the new building was started, designed by Max Bill, and the inauguration took place on October 2, 1955.” The building “remains intact today” under the Foundation Ulm. Wikipedia.

A Commons description by Martin3d says that some rooms are now used by the HfG-Archiv Ulm. Commons.

Observed

  • The volumes are low, flat-roofed boxes of bare grey concrete. They step down a grassy slope.
  • Windows run in rows of equal, nearly square panes with orange-brown wooden frames, the only warm color on the facade.
  • The entrance is a thin flat concrete canopy on two slim square posts.
  • Low concrete retaining walls and plain metal rails edge the paths.
  • The 2021 photograph shows a tall twisted stainless-steel column in the lawn. It is not identified here.

Why it belongs

The building shows the school’s method in architecture: modular parts, raw material, and no ornament. Its palette is concrete and wood, not the white and grey of the Braun products, so it fits the structure of the style more than its surface.

Borrow

Repeat one window module along a long wall, and let one warm material frame it.
